```{r setup, include=FALSE}
library(ggplot2)
options(HTTPUserAgent = "3MB001-course", timeout = 90)
use_snapshot <- TRUE
source("fetch-data.R")
```

# Question and browser evidence

Compare structural, activity and clinical-development evidence for kinase inhibition. Record PDB accessions, the organisms/constructs represented, an EGFR pathway and examples of extracellular and intracellular inhibition. Give source URLs and dates.

# Data

```{r fetch-data}
records <- fetch_target_data(use_snapshot)
activities <- records$activities
candidates <- records$candidates
records$releases
```

Mode: `r records$mode`; retrieval date: `r records$retrieved`.

```{r queries}
records$chembl_query
cat(records$opentargets_query)
```

The supplied helper uses `httr2` for GET requests to ChEMBL and a JSON GraphQL POST to Open Targets. It retries temporary failures and caches dated CSVs. It checks ChEMBL pagination and Open Targets row counts rather than silently plotting a partial result. Snapshot mode reads only the downloaded CSVs.

- ChEMBL: <https://www.ebi.ac.uk/chembl/>, CC BY-SA 3.0. This query selects imatinib (CHEMBL941), IC50 and five targets. It is not a whole-kinome panel.
- Open Targets: <https://platform.opentargets.org>, CC0. The query returns drug/candidate records and their `maxClinicalStage` for EGFR, ABL1 and KIT. This field is a **string**, not a numeric clinical phase.

# Audit before plotting

```{r audit}
with(activities, table(target, standard_relation, useNA = "ifany"))
activities[activities$target == "EGFR", c("activity_id", "standard_relation", "standard_value", "standard_units", "document_chembl_id", "assay_description")]
```

Do not replace `>` values with exact numbers or discard an inconvenient result without explaining it. In the shipped snapshot, EGFR includes one exact 0.11 nM record as well as >100000 nM and an unquantified low-inhibition record. These are conflicting assay observations, not a trustworthy pooled median. Read the source descriptions before interpreting the plot.

# Exact activity measurements

The filter below retains positive exact IC50s in nM, binding assays, records without a data-validity flag and without a potential-duplicate flag. The raw table remains available for auditing. A pChEMBL value is approximately -log10(IC50 in mol/L) here; IC50 is assay-dependent and is not a binding Kd.

```{r filter-activities}
validity_ok <- is.na(activities$data_validity_comment) | activities$data_validity_comment == ""
exact <- subset(activities, standard_relation == "=" & standard_units == "nM" &
                  standard_value > 0 & assay_type == "B" & validity_ok & potential_duplicate == 0)
exact$pic50 <- -log10(exact$standard_value * 1e-9)
```

Make a strip plot. Add a dashed horizontal line at pIC50 = 6 (1 micromolar). Label the plot as **exact values only**; SRC may have no exact values, which does not mean no one measured it.

```{r activity-plot, fig.width=8, fig.height=4.5}
ggplot(exact, aes(x = target, y = pic50)) +
  geom_jitter(width = 0.12, height = 0, alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 6, linetype = "dashed") +
  labs(x = "Annotated target", y = "pIC50 (-log10 IC50 in mol/L)",
       caption = paste("ChEMBL; retrieved", records$retrieved,
         "— exact binding-assay values only; censored records excluded from this plot")) +
  theme_minimal()
```

# Illustrative dose-response curves

Summarise exact IC50s for ABL1, KIT and PDGFRA using medians, then draw inhibition = dose / (IC50 + dose). This is a Hill-slope-1 illustration, **not a fitted clinical dose-response**. Do not pool the conflicting EGFR records into a single curve.

```{r curves, fig.width=8, fig.height=4.5}
focus <- subset(exact, target %in% c("ABL1", "KIT", "PDGFRA"))
medians <- aggregate(standard_value ~ target, focus, median)
names(medians)[2] <- "ic50_nm"
curves <- merge(medians, data.frame(dose_nm = 10^seq(-1, 5, length.out = 150)))
curves$inhibition <- curves$dose_nm / (curves$ic50_nm + curves$dose_nm)
ggplot(curves, aes(dose_nm, inhibition, colour = target)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) + scale_x_log10() +
  labs(x = "Drug concentration (nM, log scale)", y = "Illustrative fraction inhibited",
       caption = paste("ChEMBL median exact IC50; retrieved", records$retrieved,
                        "— Hill slope fixed at 1; not a fit or clinical prediction")) +
  theme_minimal()
medians
```

# A matched-source comparison

Use source document CHEMBL1130562 to compare the ABL1 record (38 nM) with the EGFR bound (>100000 nM). Inspect the assay descriptions: the ABL assay uses v-Abl; a common paper still does not guarantee identical assay conditions.

```{r matched-source}
matched <- subset(activities, document_chembl_id == "CHEMBL1130562")
matched[, c("target", "standard_relation", "standard_value", "standard_units", "assay_description")]
dose_nm <- 1000
abl_ic50 <- subset(matched, target == "ABL1" & standard_relation == "=")$standard_value
egfr_bound <- subset(matched, target == "EGFR" & standard_relation == ">")$standard_value
stopifnot(length(abl_ic50) == 1L, length(egfr_bound) == 1L)
abl_inhibition <- dose_nm / (abl_ic50 + dose_nm)
egfr_upper_bound <- dose_nm / (egfr_bound + dose_nm)
c(abl_illustration = abl_inhibition, egfr_upper_bound = egfr_upper_bound)
```

Under the stated Hill model, 1 µM gives about `r round(100 * abl_inhibition, 1)`% inhibition for the ABL record and **less than** `r round(100 * egfr_upper_bound, 2)`% for the EGFR bound. This is a comparison of those assays, not a resolution of the conflicting EGFR literature.

# Clinical development records

Count records by `target` and `stage`, then draw a bar plot. Preserve categorical stage names: `APPROVAL`, `PHASE_4` and `PHASE_2_3` are not one integer scale. Counts refer to returned records, not distinct approved drugs or independent trials.

```{r stage-plot, fig.width=8, fig.height=5}
stage_counts <- as.data.frame(table(candidates$target, candidates$stage), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
names(stage_counts) <- c("target", "stage", "records")
ggplot(stage_counts, aes(stage, records, fill = target)) +
  geom_col(position = "dodge") +
  labs(x = "Maximum clinical stage (database category)", y = "Drug/candidate records (count)",
       caption = paste("Open Targets; retrieved", records$retrieved,
                        "— records can include related formulations and multiple mechanisms")) +
  theme_minimal() + theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))
table(candidates$target)
```

# Interpretation and limits

The activity records support inhibition of several kinases, with large assay-to-assay variation. The conflicting EGFR observation deserves investigation rather than averaging into a false consensus. ABL1, KIT and PDGFRA activity connects to several disease mechanisms, but the plot does not predict patient response: exposure, tumour variants, resistance and clinical studies matter. Clinical-stage counts describe database records and are not a ranking of efficacy.
